transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [name]. Well, I'm here because... I just can't shake this feeling I've been having at work. I'm a teacher, and lately, it seems like certain staff emails or even the morning announcements are actually coded messages directed at me. My colleagues have tried to gently point out that these emails are sent to everyone, but... I just can't stop feeling like there's a hidden meaning meant only for me.
How long have you been noticing these feelings that messages are specifically directed at you?

I'd say it's been about four months now. That's when the worries about the coded messages really started. And... well, around that same time, I also started noticing a voice that I sometimes find myself answering. So, yes, it's been going on for about four months.

During these past four months, have you also noticed significant changes in your mood, like feeling very sad, hopeless, or losing interest in things, or on the other end, feeling unusually elated, energetic, or needing much less sleep?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I haven't felt hopeless or... particularly sad. And I'm definitely not unusually energetic or needing less sleep. My sleep is about the same as always. My mood has been pretty steady, honestly. It's really just the stress of trying to figure out those emails and dealing with that voice.
Have you had any recent medical illnesses, head injuries, neurological problems, or have you been using any drugs, alcohol, or new medications around the time these symptoms started?

No, nothing like that. I haven't been sick, no head injuries or anything neurological that I know of. I don't really drink, maybe a glass of wine on a special occasion, but no drugs. And I haven't started any new medications either. Physically, I've been perfectly fine.
Since these experiences started, have you noticed any changes in how well you're able to perform your job or maintain your usual relationships with friends and family?

Well, I'm still teaching, but... it has been harder. I've actually had to ask my coworkers to cover parts of my project lessons lately. And I need their help just to get through our planning meetings. I just get so distracted by everything else going on. 

As for my personal life... I guess I've pulled back a lot. I used to be really involved, but I've stopped being reliable for my book club, the theater group I go to, and even just regular neighborhood events. I just haven't had the focus or energy for them.

Before these coded-message worries started four months ago, did you notice any earlier changes—like feeling more suspicious, withdrawn, or 'off' in ways that felt unusual for you—going back further than four months?

Actually, yes, now that I think about it. The emails and all that started four months ago, but... this overall change in how I think, how I'm doing at work, and just connecting with people... that's been going on longer. 

It really started right around the time my youngest left for college. That was about a year and two months ago. So, I guess things have felt a bit off for over a year now.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports persistent referential delusions (believing coded messages in emails/announcements are directed at her) and auditory hallucinations (a voice she responds to) for 4 months, embedded within a broader prodromal decline in functioning lasting over a year since her youngest child left home. Mood symptoms (depressive or manic) were explicitly denied, ruling out a primary mood disorder with psychotic features or schizoaffective disorder. Medical, neurological, and substance-related causes were excluded. Clear functional impairment is present in both occupational (needing coworker coverage, difficulty in planning meetings) and social domains (withdrawal from book club, theater group, neighborhood events). The combination of two or more Criterion A symptoms (delusions and hallucinations) persisting with functional decline for more than 6 months meets criteria for Schizophrenia.
